#!/bin/bash
#flux: --nodes=1
#flux: --ntasks=10
#flux: --cpus-per-task=2
#flux: --mem-per-node=64G
#flux: --job-name=hundreth_spikes
#flux: --output=beegenn.stdout.txt
#flux: --error=beegenn.stderr.txt
#flux: --mail-type=ALL
#flux: --mail-user=giacomo.fantoni@studenti.unitn.it
# The PBS queue directive '-q common_cpuQ' does not have a direct equivalent in Flux.
# This is typically handled by resource constraints or queue policies on the target system.
# The PBS mail trigger '-m abe' (abort, begin, end) was translated to '--mail-type=ALL'.
# The PBS resource request 'select=1:ncpus=2:mpiprocs=10' is ambiguous. It has been interpreted
# as a request for 10 tasks (MPI processes), with 2 CPUs available to each task. This implies a
# total of 20 cores are requested, though the original may have intended only 10.

module load cuda-11.1
module load singularity-3.4.0

# The 'cd $PBS_O_WORKDIR' command is not needed as Flux starts jobs in the submission directory by default.

rm beegenn_sleep.sif

# NOTE: you need to install squashfs-tools from source, or singularity will fail!
# https://github.com/plougher/squashfs-tools/blob/master/INSTALL
# Make sure to install mksquashfs inside ~/.local so that it can be found in the PATH

singularity pull docker://giacthephantom/beegenn:sleep
# TODO: genn-network-model/data can/should be replaced with anything we want
# singularity run --bind $PBS_O_WORKDIR/genn-network-model/data:/data,$PBS_O_WORKDIR/outputs:/home/genn docker://giacthephantom/beegenn:sleep sim_docker

# WARNING: The 'singularity exec' command below is a serial command and will only run on one
# of the 10 allocated tasks. The other 9 tasks will remain idle, wasting resources.
singularity exec \
  --bind $PWD/genn-network-model/t_30_hundreth_synapses:/t_30_hundreth_synapses,$PWD/outputs:/home/genn \
  --nv \
  docker://giacthephantom/beegenn:sleep \
  python3 -m beegenn.plots.spikes /t_30_hundreth_synapses t30noinputhundrethsynapsespoissoncluster

This means that only one of the 10 allocated task slots (and its associated 2 CPUs) will be used, while the other 9 task slots (18 CPUs) will remain completely idle, resulting in a 90% waste of allocated CPU resources.
